language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Sanofi's Q3 2026 release puts its influenza and COVID-19 vaccine sales at EUR1,256m, down 18.8% at CER: US EUR911m (-13.4%), Europe EUR243m (-32.0%). It says Northern Hemisphere seasonal deliveries are phased toward Q4 this year, and its Oct 6 aide-memoire blames 'atypical strain selection timelines'. Nuvaxovid is sold by Sanofi and pays Novavax high-teens to low-twenties royalties plus supply sales. Those Sanofi lines are excluded from Novavax's revenue framework and are the unguided part of the Q3 number, which suggests Q3 Sanofi royalties and supply sales tilt low against Q3 2025, when the Sanofi line was $48m.

findings.finding: Pfizer's Q3 2026 release (Nov 3) reports US Comirnaty revenue of $562m, down 35% from $870m, 'primarily resulting from narrower vaccine recommendations'. The 2026-27 formula is approved only for adults 65+ and high-risk people aged 5-64, and there is no functioning ACIP recommendation (AJMC, 2026-10-01). This is an independent read on the US COVID vaccine market for the 2026-27 season, on which Sanofi's Nuvaxovid sales, and so Novavax's royalties and any commentary on the US season, depend. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no separable precedent. The stock fell on the Nov 2025 print (-1.3%) when COVID vaccine weakness under US policy was the theme, and the Feb 2025 print (-3.55%) also came on a weak COVID outlook.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide in the 10-19 pre-release (lower half of $300-350m) needs Q4 revenue of $92-117m against Q3's $82-83m: an 11-42% sequential step-up, in the quarter Line 1 consolidates into Thorn Hill and the final shift is added. Street FY of about $309m implies Q4 of about $101m. The guide has already been cut once (Aug: $300-400m to $300-350m) and then moved to the lower half (Oct). A third trim below $300m, or soft Q4/2027 commentary on the call, is the main downside line. Reaffirming the low end three weeks into Q4 is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 5, 2026 full release cut the FY guide after the July pre-release had already given revenue: -12.18% on the day and -46.9% drift since (Earnings Whispers). Feb 26, 2026: Q4 revenue miss and weak outlook, -39.44%. When the July pre-release gave no guide, the stock moved +1.86%; the 10-19 pre-release that set 'lower half' moved -0.55%.

findings.finding: Q3 cash fell only $20m to about $344m, and only because of an $87.0m DOE advance (funded 2026-09-10) and $114m of operating inflows from deposits, milestones and tax-credit collections. Ex-DOE, the drawdown was about $107m in the quarter, including $35m capex. About $99.5m of the $277.5m DOE facility remains, and the Cerberus credit agreement carries a $15m minimum-liquidity covenant. The company has raised repeatedly: a $225m convert, and a $150m rights offering in July 2026. A new raise or financing announced with or around the release is a live possibility. Asked what it would buy: a ramp that is real in revenue (+20% QoQ) but still loses about 54 cents of gross margin per revenue dollar, while backlog fell QoQ. So the sign is mildly negative, not distress: there is no going-concern language in the Q2 10-Q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026 rights offering: Stifel cut its target $12 to $10 (Jul 13, https://finviz.com/news/367612/eos-energy-shares-edge-lower-after-stifel-reduces-price-target-following-capital-raise-eose). An earlier $225m convert pricing saw the stock 'slide further' (Seeking Alpha headline, https://seekingalpha.com/news/4453809-eos-energy-slides-further-after-pricing-225-million-convertible-note-offering, undated in snippet). No financing was announced on any of the print days in the baseline.

findings.finding: Q3 GAAP net income will carry a large non-cash fair-value gain. The stock fell from $5.88 (Jun 30) to $3.06 (Sep 30), and the warrant liabilities ($135.4m plus $254.0m related-party at Jun 30) and derivative liabilities are marked to the period-end price. In Q2 a 19% rise cost about $184m of fair-value losses; in Q1 a 57% fall produced $601.9m of gains and diluted EPS of +$0.12. The headline GAAP EPS is therefore likely far above the -$0.37 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (May 13): net income $508.9m from fair-value gains, a GAAP 'beat' against a loss consensus; the stock moved +2.22% on the day and gapped down the next (MarketBeat 2026-05-14). The market looked through it.

findings.finding: Backlog fell from a record $807m (Jun 30) to about $765m (Sep 30), so book-to-bill was below 1. The pre-release also says a $100m order under the existing FPUSA capacity reservation did not add to QoQ backlog growth. The call will be asked for order flow; the falling backlog is already public.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's record backlog (+25% QoQ) arrived with the guide cut, and the stock fell -12.18%: the backlog did not carry the print. The 10-19 pre-release with a lower backlog moved -0.55%.

findings.finding: This is a crowded short going into a print whose numbers are mostly pre-released. 139.3m shares were short at 10-15 (about 38% of shares outstanding, rising for three straight settlements; 4.7 days to cover), and the float is much smaller because Cerberus holds about 35%. The 25-delta skew is -30 vol points (upside paid). The stock has bounced about 24% off its $1.82 low (10-28) into the print. Absent a new negative such as a guide trim or a raise, a 'no surprise' release gives shorts a reason to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 9, 2026: +29.63% (baseline, 8-K 2.02 day). The stock spiked about 20% intraday that day (low-quality auto-generated page, used only for the date), showing the name can squeeze. Equibles' screening index rates the squeeze score 73/100, which is not a probability.

findings.finding: Q3 gross margin of -53% to -55% improved 16-18 points QoQ, the eighth straight improvement. The CFO says there is 'a clear path to positive margins', and consolidation into Thorn Hill (final shift in Q4) is said to lower cost per unit. If the full release or call dates positive gross margin, say Q4 2026 or H1 2027, that is the one unambiguous upside line still unpublished.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin improvement has printed every quarter: Q1 -78%, Q2 -71%, Q3 about -54%. The stock still fell on two of the three full releases this year. Earnings Whispers notes the positive-margin target has slipped repeatedly, so the market has learned to discount it.

findings.finding: Revenue quality: in Q2, $55.0m of $68.8m (80%) was related-party revenue from a project contributed to Frontier Power USA. FPUSA is the Cerberus/Hudson Bay JV in which Eos holds a minority stake. It also held about half of backlog, and the $100m Blanquilla PO came under its capacity reservation. The Q3 10-Q will show how much of the $82-83m is again related-party, which the pre-release does not disclose.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 release disclosed the 80% related-party share alongside the guide cut, and the stock fell -12.18%. The effect of each item alone is not separable.

findings.finding: Insider and management churn: CCO Michelle Buczkowski sold 50,000 shares at a $2.00 weighted average on 2026-10-29 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-12-11 to cover RSU tax withholding. Outgoing CCO Nathan Kroeker left on 2026-10-20. Neither is an informative signal on the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None identifiable.

outside_window.finding: Resale overhang: an S-3ASR (2026-08-31) registers 56.5m shares for resale by Cerberus (37.4m) and Hudson Bay (19.1m) from the Frontier warrants, exchange rights and Series B conversion. Hudson Bay is a typical seller. This is a supply overhang with no dated catalyst in the window.
The next FINRA short-interest release (10-30 settlement) is due 2026-11-10, after the exit window.

lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (finding inside the company's guide): the Q4/FY guidance finding is shrunk from -1.5 to -0.8, because the 'lower half' guide was given three weeks before the print.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): what would a raise buy? A real revenue ramp (+20% QoQ) at -54% gross margin with backlog down. No going concern, so the sign is mildly negative, not distress; -1.5 to -0.8. Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives) is folded into that same single cut, not stacked.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the GAAP fair-value gain is below the line with no path to the guide; +0.5 to +0.3, and the Q1 precedent (+2.22%) is cited.
Lesson 1 (a fact is not a reaction): the pre-released backlog decline is shrunk from -0.5 to -0.3, and the margin path from +0.5 to +0.3 because the target has slipped before.
Lesson 9 (net of the rest): the related-party concentration finding is sized net of six non-FPUSA customer POs; -0.5 to -0.4.
Lesson 7 left the positioning finding standing at +2.0, and moved p_up from 48 to 51 together with the shrunk negatives.
'A reaction history built from the wrong events': the base rate was rebuilt from confirmed full releases (see rejected_candidates).

findings.finding: Chime reset its own Q3 guide on 2026-09-08, about two-thirds into the quarter, to revenue ~$705m (from $680-690m) and adj. EBITDA $117-120m (from $105-110m); consensus $705.2m sits exactly on it. On the last print the company beat its own revenue guide midpoint by ~5% ($670m vs $633-643m guide), but a guide set with two months of the quarter in hand leaves room for only a ~1-2% beat (~$710-720m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-05): revenue $670m vs $633-643m guide, with a FY raise, stock +20.56%. Q1 2026 (2026-05-06): revenue $647m, FY raised, but stock -12.52% (next-quarter EBITDA guide $72-77m vs $119m Q1). Beats on this line have been bought or sold depending on the guide, not on the beat.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide of $2.76-2.77bn revenue and $481-489m adj. EBITDA, less Q1 ($647m / $119m), Q2 ($670m / $102m) and the Q3 guide ($705m / $117-120m), implies Q4 revenue of $738-748m (~26% y/y, a deceleration from ~30% in Q3) and Q4 adj. EBITDA of ~$140-151m, a ~19-20% margin against 15-17% in Q2-Q3. The Q4 guide must hold a steep EBITDA ramp; the 10% workforce reduction and easing Prime cash-back rewards cost support it, but a Q4 EBITDA guide below the implied ramp is the setup that cost -12.5% after Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: FY revenue raised but next-quarter EBITDA guide implied margin compression, stock -12.52%. Q4 2025 print (2026-02-25): 2026 outlook above expectations, +13.55%. Q2 2026: third FY raise, +20.56%. The guide line has decided the sign on every print in the baseline.

findings.finding: Chime agreed on 2026-09-08 to buy partner bank Stride Bank for $590m cash (~1.5x tangible book), immediately EPS-accretive with >$100m of net synergies (partner-bank fees and funding costs), closing H1 2027 subject to OCC/Fed approval; the call is the first chance to quantify synergy timing and any 2027 framing, while the company says it will keep assets under $10bn to preserve the Durbin exemption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement itself moved the stock ~+10% after hours and ~+11% premarket on 2026-09-09 (https://www.americanbanker.com/payments/news/chime-to-buy-longtime-partner-stride-bank-for-590-million). No prior print has carried this line.

findings.finding: SoFi's Q3 2026 release (late October, after Chime last spoke) showed a record 1.2m member adds to 17.1m (+35% y/y), deposits +$5.8bn q/q to $51.3bn, Financial Services revenue +25%, a raised FY guide and a 2027 outlook above estimates: the closest listed consumer-fintech peer saw no slowdown in Q3 member acquisition or deposit demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of Chime reacting to peer prints; Chime's member-add line drove the +20.56% Q2 reaction (record 1.7m net adds over 12 months).

findings.finding: The Bancorp (TBBK), one of Chime's two partner banks, reported on 2026-10-29 Q3 gross dollar volume on prepaid, debit and credit cards of $54.3bn vs $44.0bn a year earlier (+23%), fintech-fee-driven EPS of $1.53, and average deposits $8.42bn, flat q/q; card volume growth in the low 20s is consistent with Chime's purchase-volume trend, flat deposits a mild caution.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record; Chime's purchase-volume line was cited in the +20.56% Q2 reaction.

findings.finding: Visa's fiscal Q4 2026 release (2026-10-27) showed payments volume +9% in constant dollars and management described October volume growth as relatively stable: no sign of a broad US consumer-spending slowdown into Chime's quarter-end and Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline.

findings.finding: The stock ran +6.58% intraday on the print day itself (to $30.06 at 13:02 ET, from $28.20), +4.86% over 5 days and +8.13% over 20, into a +10.65 vol-point put skew; with short interest a moderate 7.58% of float (5.8 days to cover, falling), the run-up raises the bar for the guide without a squeeze cushion of size.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No run-up-conditioned history in the baseline; the two largest down reactions (-14.68%, -12.52%) came on guide disappointments.

findings.finding: Insiders have sold about $1.2bn across 112 filings over 12 months with no open-market purchases; October sales were small 10b5-1 trades by co-founder Ryan King (50,000 shares at ~$29.40 on 2026-10-09; 11,318 at $31.03 on 2026-10-20 under a plan adopted 2025-08-28), CEO Britt sold under a plan in late August/early September.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline.

findings.finding: Q3 GAAP results carry $16-20m of net cash restructuring charges from the ~10% workforce cut (partly offset by a $9-12m SBC reversal, net income hit $6-9m, roughly $0.02 a share), excluded from adj. EBITDA; a GAAP EPS headline against the $0.09 consensus could read light if estimates do not include it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print carried a restructuring charge.

findings.finding: Credit is the watch line in the quarter: MyPay limits were raised to $1,000 with management expecting loss rates to tick up modestly (Q2 MyPay loss rate 0.9% on $4.5bn originations), and Instant Loans (originations +70% q/q to $300m in Q2) are guided to exit Q3 above a $100m revenue run rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No credit miss in the baseline; Compass Point initiated at Neutral citing credit risk (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/chime-initiated-with-a-neutral-at-compass-point-on-credit-risk-thefly), undated in results.

findings.finding: The CFO seat is still interim (Mark Troughton, President and interim CFO since 2026-08-07 after Matt Newcomb left); a permanent appointment or its absence may be addressed on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CFO departure was announced with the Q2 print, which rose 20.56%.

outside_window.finding: Stride Bank acquisition closing and OCC/Fed approval expected H1 2027; synergies (>$100m net) accrue after close.

Durbin / Regulation II litigation (Corner Post vacatur stayed pending appeal; Fed 2023 proposal to cut the cap to 14.4c) does not touch Chime directly while it and its partner banks stay under $10bn in assets; no ruling dated in the window.
